clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Classification performance evaluation (Balanced Accuracy (BACC), Specificity (SPE), Sensitivity (SEN), Area Under the Curve (AUC)); comparison with normative model-based strategy, deep learning methods, and classical machine learning methods (SVM, LASSO).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: The proposed Hippocampal-Amygdalo-Ventricular Atrophy score (HAVAs) method demonstrated very accurate detection of AD and discrimination of progressive MCI, outperforming other normative modeling, classical machine learning, and deep learning methods.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: The study introduced the Hippocampal-Amygdalo-Ventricular Atrophy score (HAVAs), a novel MRI-based method for AD detection and MCI prognosis, derived from normative and pathological lifespan models. HAVAs achieved high classification performance on external validation datasets, demonstrating accurate detection of AD patients (AUC ≥ 94%) and discrimination of progressive MCI (AUC = 78%). Specifically, for AD vs. CN diagnosis, HAVAs showed 88% BACC and 94% AUC on AIBL, and 89% BACC and 96% AUC on MIRIAD. For sMCI vs. pMCI prognosis, it achieved 73% BACC and 78% AUC on ADNI. HAVAs consistently outperformed normative modeling, classical machine learning, and deep learning methods, showing an improvement of 3 percentage points over the second-best methods for both diagnosis and prognosis. The simplicity and interpretability of HAVAs make it suitable for clinical practice.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: HAVAs is presented as a simple, interpretable, and computationally efficient method with a low number of parameters and hyperparameters, making it well-suited for clinical practice and pharmaceutical trials. A software package and online platform will be made freely available.
